newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria tells visiting Israelis it seeks peace.
newsitem.headline: Syria tells visiting Israelis it seeks peace.

text.p: Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara assured 44 visiting Israeli Arabs, including members of parliament, that Syria is still seeking peace despite the policies of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

"The minister told us that he was optimistic despite all conditions...although he said there were not signs of hope with the presence of Netanyahu's government," Saleh Tarif told reporters the morning after Monday evening's dinner meeting.

Tarif, a Labour party member of the Israeli parliament, said he was carrying a call to coordinate peace efforts from Israeli Labour party leader Ehud Barak to the Syrian leadership. He did not give details.
The visit -- only the second such delegation to Damascus in 50 years -- coincided with U.S. envoy Dennis Ross's mission to Israel to revive Israeli-Palestinian peace talks, frozen since March.
"I am not optimistic at all about the results of the visit of Ross to the region," Fayez Abbas, correspondent of the Israeli daily Yedioth Ahronoth, quoted Shara as saying.

"The responsibility of blocking the peace process and escalating tension is Netanyahu's and his government...yet, despite all difficulties, I feel optimistic about all that is related to the peace process because it is the future," Shara said.
The Israeli delegation, which includes members of the opposition Labour and Meretz parties, arrived in Damascus via Egypt on Friday at the invitation of Syrian President Hafez al-Assad.

Sporadic Syrian-Israeli peace talks have failed to resume since the May 1996 election of Netanyahu, who has rejected Syrian demands for return of the Golan Heights that Israel captured in 1967. The former Labour government had been willing to trade at least part of the strategic plateau for peace.

Delegates quoted Shara as saying Israel's previous Labour government was committed to full withdrawal from the Golan. He said an agreement had not emerged because Israel wanted a "hasty" normalisation of ties.
Tarif said Shara noted the moderate policies of the Israeli left and "optimism could be possible with its presence and that it was possible to reach solutions with it".

He quoted Shara as saying Arabs in Israel "are a strong power that could affect inside and outside (Israel) and from today the situation which existed before of boycotting Israeli Arab leaderships would be corrected and they will have a direct contact with Syria and other Arab countries".
The delegates, including writers and journalists who said they came to show support with Syria's demand for the Golan and improve cooperation with Syria, said they would meet Assad on Tuesday.
Ibrahim Nemer Hussein, head of the delegation, said talks with Assad would cover cooperation and ways to hold an Arab summit about Netanyahu's policies.
